methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Late Stage → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $575M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 10 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
VulcanForms is a late-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by John Hart and Martin Feldmann that has raised $575M+ to date. The valuation universe comprises ten same-sector peers: one public company (277810.KQ) and nine private firms including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics. However, the peer set lacks sufficient narrow-stage and valuation-tier overlap to support a reliable peer-median approach.

Given data constraints, stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($575M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical of late-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $690M. This method assumes forward progression within the late-stage band and reasonable multiple compression relative to early-stage capital intensity.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $586M to $793M, centered at $690M. The lower and upper bounds reflect ±15% sensitivity around the point estimate. Key uncertainties include the absence of comparable late-stage robotics transactions in the private dataset, preventing market-rate validation, and reliance on stage-progression heuristics rather than transaction multiples or revenue-based metrics. A more robust valuation would require either disclosure of financial performance or identification of additional late-stage comparables.
